newsitem.title: CANADA: TENNIS-SCHULTZ-MCCARTHY BEGINS QUEBEC TITLE DEFENSE WITH WIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SCHULTZ-MCCARTHY BEGINS QUEBEC TITLE DEFENSE WITH WIN.

text.p: Top seed Brenda Schultz-McCarthy began defence of her title at the Bell Challenge tennis tournament with a first-round victory on Wednesday.
The 11th-ranked Dutchwoman got off to a slow start before powering her way to a 7-6 6-2 victory over Stephanie De Ville of Belgium.
In second-round action, fifth-seeded American Lisa Raymond and sixth seed Florencia Labat of Argentina posted straight sets victories.
But third seed Amy Frazier was upended by unheralded Els Callens of Belgium 3-6 6-2 6-4.
The 73rd-ranked Callens earned a quarter-final meeting with Labat, who ousted Canadian Patricia Hy-Boulais 7-5 6-3.
Raymond booked her quarter-final passage with a 7-5 6-2 victory over compatriot Debbie Graham, whose ranking has dropped more than 100 places since 1992.
"I've been going, going, going the last three months trying to get my ranking back up," said a dejected Graham, now a lowly 138th in the world.
A travel-weary Schultz-McCarthy arrived in Quebec City from her Florida home Tuesday after flying from Zurich to Florida on Monday.
"Getting here late wasn't exactly perfect for me," she said in explaining her sluggish start.
"But I played a good tie-break and then I started serving really well in the second set."
The big-serving Schultz-McCarthy took the breaker 7-3 before dominating the second set.
Callens, nursing a pulled stomach muscle, surprisingly turned her game up a notch against the 26th-ranked Frazier following a second-set timeout to tend to a thigh injury.
"I was too worried about my stomach," she said. "But after the injury break I decided to forget everything and go for broke. That's when I started playing better."
